chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, and Ḥusayn ibn Hāshim, and ʿAlī ibn Ribāṭ, and Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the salat of ẓuhr, and he said: “When the shadow is one cubit.” I said: One cubit from what? He said: “One cubit from your shadow.” I said: Then ʿaṣr? He said: “Half of that.” I said: This is a span. He said: “A span—is not a span much?”
So if it is said: We see that you have arranged the times in relation to one another and made some of them have merit over others, while it has been narrated that all of that is equal.

key_terms.الشَّطْرُ: half; here, half of the previous measure
key_terms.الْفَيْءُ: the returning shadow used here as a measure for prayer time
key_terms.ذِرَاعًا: a cubit; a unit of length used to define time by shadow
key_terms.شِبْرٌ: a span; a smaller hand-based unit of measure
key_terms.فَيْئِكَ: your shadow; the measured shadow in reference to the person

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the timing of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr salat by shadow length?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timing of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr salat by reference to the measure of shadow. It indicates a graded arrangement of prayer times and points to distinctions of merit between them. The closing sentence introduces an objection about reports that suggest all those times are equal.
